intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Witness the breathtaking sunrise over the iconic Angkor Wat temple complex, one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Explore the intricate bas-reliefs and towering spires that tell the story of the ancient Khmer Empire. A guided tour helps uncover the rich history and symbolism carved into every stone.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Beachfront Snorkeling & Island Hopping
experiences.description: Spend a day exploring the crystal-clear turquoise waters surrounding Koh Rong island. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs, discover secluded white-sand beaches, and hop between nearby islets. Evening bioluminescent plankton experiences make this a truly magical coastal adventure.

experiences.name: Sihanoukville Khmer Seafood Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef near the beachfront for an immersive Khmer cooking class focused on fresh coastal seafood. Learn to prepare traditional dishes like Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and grilled crab with Kampot pepper. Includes a visit to the local market to select fresh ingredients and a beachside meal to enjoy your creations.

experiences.name: Otres Beach Sunset Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle along the calm, scenic coastline of Otres Beach at golden hour, taking in stunning views of the Gulf of Thailand. Explore hidden mangrove channels and quiet coves accessible only by kayak. This peaceful activity offers a perfect blend of nature, relaxation, and coastal beauty.

experiences.name: Kampot Riverside Cultural Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore the charming colonial-era town of Kampot on a guided walking tour along the riverside. Discover French colonial architecture, vibrant street art, Buddhist temples, and local pepper farms that have made Kampot pepper world-famous. Interact with local artisans and sample traditional Cambodian snacks at riverside stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take a tuk-tuk (~$5-7) to your boutique stay in the Angkor Archaeological Park area. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk around the immediate neighborhood to get oriented. Visit the nearby Angkor Night Market area for a gentle first look at local life.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chaa) area in Siem Reap town center (~15-20 min tuk-tuk from hotel). Browse local handicrafts and soak in the atmosphere. Watch a free traditional Apsara dance performance preview often staged outside restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite at the airport or a local noodle stall near the hotel for ~$2-3.
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — try amok fish curry and rice for ~$4-6. Very popular with budget travelers.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) tonight or first thing tomorrow morning at the Angkor ticket office. Carry USD cash as it is widely accepted. Arrange a tuk-tuk driver for the next few days (~$12-15/day) — many hotel staff can recommend reliable drivers.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (5:00 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise — one of the most breathtaking experiences in Southeast Asia. Watch the sun rise over the main temple reflecting in the lotus ponds. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. Spend 2-3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Angkor Wat, head to Angkor Thom complex (~2 km north). Visit the South Gate with its massive stone faces, the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon Temple, Phimeanakas, and the Elephant Terrace. Have lunch near the ticket checkpoint area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest during the hottest part of the day, then visit Pre Rup temple at sunset (~5:30 PM) for panoramic views over the jungle canopy. Return to Siem Reap town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a baguette and coffee from a local street vendor near Angkor Wat entrance (~$1.50) — a legacy of French colonial influence.
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice) for ~$3-4.
meals.dinner: Mie Cafe near Old Market — affordable Khmer noodle soups and stir-fries for ~$3-5.

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen, a hat, and a reusable water bottle. Temple dress code requires covered shoulders and knees — carry a scarf. Start as early as possible to beat the heat and crowds. Day 1 of your 3-day Angkor Pass.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the famous 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically engulfed by massive silk-cotton and strangler fig tree roots. Arrive early (~7:30 AM) before tour groups arrive. Then explore nearby Banteay Kdei and the peaceful Srah Srang reservoir, perfect for a quiet morning reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Preah Khan temple, a sprawling jungle monastery with long corridors, carved lintels, and atmospheric overgrown sections. Less crowded than main temples. Afterward, visit Neak Pean, a small artificial island temple, and Ta Som with its iconic tree-covered eastern gopura gateway.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor National Museum (~$12 entry) near your hotel area for historical context on the Khmer Empire — excellent exhibits on the gods, kings, and art of Angkor. Browse the night market afterward for souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local $1.50 rice porridge (bobor) from a street stall near the temple complex.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local market stall — fresh spring rolls, grilled corn, and coconut water for ~$3.
meals.dinner: Bugs Cafe (adventurous option) or Sugar Palm Restaurant — try Khmer red curry with jasmine rice for ~$5-6.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 of your 3-day Angkor Pass. Ta Prohm gets very crowded midday — go early or late afternoon. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day to cover the spread-out eastern and northern temple groups efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Use your final day of the Angkor Pass for the remote and rarely visited Banteay Srei temple (~25 km north of Siem Reap). Known as the 'Citadel of Women,' it features extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered the finest in all of Angkor. Visit the nearby Kbal Spean river carvings if time permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return toward Siem Reap and visit the Landmine Museum (~$5 donation), a sobering and important cultural site documenting Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing clearance efforts. Then explore the War Museum Cambodia for additional historical perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxing evening at a traditional Khmer cooking class (~$15-20) offered by several local schools near Siem Reap — learn to make amok, papaya salad, and spring rolls, and eat your creations for dinner.

meals.breakfast: French-style baguette with pâté from a local bakery near the hotel for ~$2 — a popular Cambodian breakfast.
meals.lunch: Local noodle soup (kuy teav) at a roadside stall near Banteay Srei for ~$2.
meals.dinner: Your cooking class meal! Typically included in the class fee.

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 of your 3-day Angkor Pass — use it wisely. Banteay Srei requires a longer tuk-tuk ride (~45 min each way, negotiate ~$15-18 round trip for the day). The Landmine Museum is sobering but essential for understanding modern Cambodian history.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Phnom Kulen National Park (~50 km from Siem Reap, $20 entry). This sacred mountain plateau is where Jayavarman II declared the Khmer Empire in 802 AD. See the River of a Thousand Lingas (carved sandstone riverbed), a large reclining Buddha, and refreshing jungle waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Phnom Kulen — swim in the cool natural pools beneath the waterfalls (a wonderful budget-friendly activity). Return to Siem Reap by late afternoon. Visit the vibrant Psar Leu local market for authentic shopping away from tourist prices.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free Phare Cambodian Circus performance preview or purchase a ticket (~$18-38) for an incredible acrobatic and storytelling show that supports at-risk Cambodian youth — a truly unique cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Rice and egg breakfast from a local stall near the hotel for ~$1.50.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for Phnom Kulen, or buy grilled meats and fresh fruit from vendors near the park entrance for ~$3-4.
meals.dinner: Haven Restaurant (social enterprise training disadvantaged youth) — excellent Khmer food for ~$6-8.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Kulen requires a tuk-tuk or motorbike taxi — negotiate a full-day rate (~$20-25). The road is steep and rough. Bring insect repellent, good walking shoes, and a swimsuit for the waterfall pools. The park is considered sacred — dress respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (~5-6 hours, $6-10 with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express). Depart around 7:00-7:30 AM. Enjoy the Cambodian countryside views along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early afternoon. Check into a budget guesthouse near Riverside (~$8-15/night). After dropping bags, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (~$10 entry) — stunning Khmer royal architecture with the famous Emerald Buddha and silver-tiled floor.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade at sunset — a beautiful spot to watch boats on the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Explore the lively riverside area with street food vendors and local cafes.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near Siem Reap bus station — rice porridge or baguette for ~$1.50-2.
meals.lunch: Bus stop lunch break or packed snacks (~$2-3).
meals.dinner: Riverside street food stalls near Sisowath Quay — grilled skewers, fresh spring rolls, and iced sugar cane juice for ~$4-5.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance — Giant Ibis and Mekong Express are the most reliable and comfortable budget options. Store valuables securely on the bus. Phnom Penh budget guestthouse recommendations: Mad Monkey Hostel, Onederz Hostel (~$8-15). The Royal Palace closes 11:00-14:00 for lunch.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison, ~$3 entry) — a former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. A deeply sobering but essential visit to understand Cambodia's tragic recent history. Allow 2 hours for a respectful and thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$8-10 round trip) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from center, $6 entry including audio guide). The audio guide is excellent and deeply moving. Pay respects at the memorial stupa. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia (~$10) for Khmer art and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome building. Browse for local crafts, clothing, and souvenirs at local prices. Enjoy the buzzing evening atmosphere around the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Num pang (Cambodian baguette sandwich) from a street vendor near your guesthouse for ~$1-1.50.
meals.lunch: Friends Restaurant (social enterprise) near the National Museum — excellent Khmer tapas-style dishes for ~$5-7.
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant (social enterprise, former street children) — traditional Cambodian cuisine including the famous fried tarantulas for adventurous eaters, ~$6-10.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — take your time and be respectful. Photography is allowed but be mindful. Avoid visiting these sites if you are emotionally sensitive. The audio guide at Choeung Ek (~$3) is highly recommended for context.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, $6-9). Depart by 7:00-8:00 AM. From Sihanoukville, take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (~45 min, $25 round trip) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and less commercialized islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on Koh Rong Samloem and check into a budget beach bungalow on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay (~$15-25/night). Spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear turquoise water, snorkeling around coral reefs, and relaxing on the white sand beach. Rent snorkel gear (~$3-5).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular sunset from the beach. After dark, experience the magical bioluminescent plankton — wade into the shallow water and watch the water glow blue around your movements. A truly unforgettable free natural phenomenon.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near Phnom Penh bus station or on the ferry.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a beachside shack on Koh Rong Samloem — grilled fish with rice for ~$5-7.
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Saracen Bay — seafood BBQ platter with garlic butter and steamed rice for ~$8-10.

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during peak season. Koh Rong Samloem has limited ATMs — bring sufficient USD cash. M'Pai Bay is quieter and more budget-friendly than Saracen Bay. Bioluminescence is best seen on moonless nights — check the lunar calendar. Bring insect repellent for the evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Full day on Koh Rong Samloem. Wake up early for a sunrise walk along the beach before the day heats up. Rent a kayak (~$5/hour) and paddle around the island's coastline, exploring hidden coves and mangrove channels. Visit the small fishing village on the island for a glimpse of local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget snorkeling trip (~$10-15) organized by local boat operators to nearby coral reefs and the marine sanctuary. Spot colorful fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. Alternatively, hike the jungle trail across the island to the less-visited Sunset Beach for a quieter afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on the island — enjoy a beachside dinner with fresh catch of the day. Watch the stars from the beach (minimal light pollution makes for incredible stargazing). Pack bags for the return journey tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes and fresh fruit from a beach shack for ~$3 — a classic Southeast Asia backpacker breakfast.
meals.lunch: Coconut and fresh fruit from a beach vendor (~$2), or a light noodle soup at a local eatery for ~$3.
meals.dinner: Fresh lobster or whole grilled snapper at a beachfront restaurant — splurge slightly for ~$10-12 as a memorable final island meal.

day_by_day.notes: November is generally a good month for Cambodian beaches — dry season is beginning. Water visibility for snorkeling is usually excellent. Apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. Stay hydrated — the sun is very strong even in November.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville (~45 min). From Sihanoukville, take a bus back toward Phnom Penh or directly to your departure airport depending on your flight. If time permits before departure, visit Otres Beach near Sihanoukville — a quieter, more laid-back beach compared to the main town, good for a final swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: If returning to Phnom Penh for a flight: arrive and head to the airport. Allow 2 hours before your flight for check-in. Browse the airport duty-free for last-minute Cambodian souvenirs like Kampot pepper, silk scarves, and Angkor beer. If your flight is the next day, explore Phnom Penh's Bassac Lane craft beer scene or the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) for final souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final evening in Phnom Penh. Reflect on an incredible 10 days exploring Cambodia's temples, history, culture, and beaches. Enjoy a final Cambodian meal before heading home.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the island before the ferry — toast and eggs for ~$2-3.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near Sihanoukville port or at a roadside stop — BBQ chicken skewers and sticky rice for ~$2-3.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or a final Phnom Penh dinner at a local Khmer restaurant — try a farewell bowl of kuy teav noodle soup for ~$2-3.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 10 days: Accommodation $80-150, Transport $50-70, Food $80-120, Entrance fees $80-100, Activities $40-60, Miscellaneous $30-50. Total estimated budget: $360-550 USD for 10 days. Always negotiate tuk-tuk fares before getting in. Keep small USD bills for tips and small purchases. Cambodia is generally very safe for budget travelers but keep valuables secure in busy areas.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After freshening up, take a leisurely stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby area to get oriented. Visit the Angkor National Museum (about 15 minutes from most Angkor-area hotels) for an excellent introduction to Khmer history and the temples you'll explore over the coming days.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap's Old Market (Phsar Chas) area for a gentle first evening. Explore the vibrant Pub Street neighborhood and surrounding alleys. Watch a short traditional Apsara dance performance — many restaurants offer these free during dinner hours.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the hotel or a nearby café such as Café Central near the Old Market — try a Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) for around $4–6.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or Cuisine Wat Damnak (book ahead) for authentic Khmer cuisine. Budget $12–20 per person. Try amok (fish curry in banana leaf) and lok lak (stir-fried beef).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) at the official ticket office before 17:30 on Day 1 — it can be used starting the next morning and is valid for any 3 days within a week. Bring passport photos or they'll take a digital photo on-site. Cash (USD) is widely accepted.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:00–5:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Watch the temple's reflection shimmer in the reflecting pools as dawn breaks — one of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking sights. Spend the morning (until ~10:00 AM) exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. Hire a licensed guide at the entrance ($25–35) for rich historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning break, visit the walled city of Angkor Thom. Explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Take a tuk-tuk between sites (~$15–20 for a half-day circuit). Rest at the hotel during the hottest hours (noon–2:00 PM) if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Browse the Angkor Night Market for souvenirs, silk scarves, and handmade crafts. Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage ($10–15/hour) at one of the reputable spas near Pub Street.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack or coffee at the hotel before sunrise. Many hotels offer packed breakfasts for temple visits.
meals.lunch: Picnic snacks from a nearby vendor inside the park, or eat at one of the open-air restaurants near Angkor Thom's south gate — try a fresh coconut ($1) and a rice dish ($4–6).
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Sugar Palm or Viroth's Restaurant in Siem Reap — excellent mid-range Khmer dining at $10–18 per person. Try samlor korko (vegetable and pork soup).

day_by_day.notes: November is ideal weather for Cambodia — dry season begins, with temperatures around 28–32°C. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 2 liters of water. Modest dress (covered shoulders and knees) is required at all temple sites. This counts as Day 1 of your 3-day Angkor Pass.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle-clad temple of Ta Prohm — famously left partially unrestored with massive silk-cotton tree roots embracing its walls (the 'Tomb Raider' temple). Arrive early (7:30–8:00 AM) before tour groups arrive. Nearby, visit Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir, perfect for quiet reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pre Rup and East Mebon temples — slightly further from the main circuit but less crowded and architecturally stunning. In the late afternoon, head to Banteay Srei (about 25 km north of Angkor), a 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings and delicate bas-reliefs. Often called the 'Jewel of Khmer Art.'
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Phnom Bakheng hill temple (note: timed tickets required — book in advance at the Angkor Pass office). The hilltop offers panoramic views over the jungle canopy toward Angkor Wat. Return to town for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel (most boutique stays include breakfast). Alternatively, try a local bakery near the Old Market for a baguette with eggs — a French-Cambodian colonial legacy, around $3–5.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the local restaurants near Banteay Srei village — simple Khmer rice dishes and fresh fruit for $4–7.
meals.dinner: Try Mie Café or Sister Srey Café in Siem Reap for a relaxed atmosphere. Budget $8–15 per person. Enjoy a mango shake and Khmer red curry.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a tuk-tuk or private car — negotiate a full-day hire ($25–35). Phnom Bakheng sunset tickets are limited; secure yours at the Angkor Visitor Center before heading out in the morning. This is Day 2 of your Angkor Pass.

day_by_day.morning: Use your final Angkor Pass day to visit the lesser-explored but magnificent Preah Khan temple — a vast monastic complex with long corridors, carved lintels, and a peaceful jungle atmosphere. Follow with nearby Neak Pean, an artificial island temple set in a pond, and Ta Som, a small but charming jungle-wrapped temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a midday rest. In the afternoon, visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique in Siem Reap — a social enterprise training disadvantaged Cambodians in traditional silk weaving, stone carving, and lacquerware. Free to visit and a wonderful cultural insight. Browse their fair-trade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a full Apsara dance performance at the Apsara Theatre or Angkor Village Theatre ($15–25 per person). These elaborate performances showcase classical Khmer dance, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, with stunning costumes and live traditional music.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab bánh mì-style sandwiches from a street vendor near the Old Market ($1.50–2).
meals.lunch: Dine at Bugs Café (adventurous!) or a more conventional spot like Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — $6–10 per person.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at Angkor Village Resort's restaurant or a nearby spot. Post-show, grab a dessert crepe or fresh fruit smoothie from a street stall.

day_by_day.notes: This is Day 3 and the final day of your Angkor Pass. If you'd like to revisit any temples, use this day strategically. Consider hiring a knowledgeable licensed guide for Preah Khan — the history of this temple as a university-monastery is fascinating.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the floating villages of Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Take a boat tour through Kampong Phluk (preferred over Chong Khneas for authenticity), a stilted village community whose houses tower 6–8 meters above water level in dry season. Observe daily life, fishing communities, and flooded mangrove forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Tonlé Sap by early afternoon. Visit the Cambodian Cultural Village on the outskirts of Siem Reap for a broad overview of Cambodia's diverse ethnic groups, traditional architecture, and folk performances — good for cultural context before traveling south.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Siem Reap. Walk along the Siem Reap River promenade. Visit the Made in Cambodia Market (open evenings near the Old Market) for last-minute quality souvenirs — silk, ceramics, and ethical crafts.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the Tonlé Sap departure (boats often leave by 7:30–8:00 AM).
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — an authentic experience at $6–10. Try prahok (fermented fish paste) dishes if adventurous.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly at Embassy Restaurant or Cuisine Wat Damnak (if not visited on Day 1) for a refined Cambodian tasting menu — $20–35 per person. A worthy send-off from Siem Reap.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonlé Sap boat tour through your hotel or a reputable agency ($15–25 per person). Kampong Phluk tours typically take 3–4 hours including transfer. In November, water levels are still relatively high, making boat navigation easier and more scenic. Prepare to travel south tomorrow — pack your bags tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap for Phnom Penh by express bus or domestic flight. The bus takes approximately 6 hours ($12–15) and offers scenic countryside views; a flight takes 45 minutes ($40–80). If taking the bus, depart by 7:00–8:00 AM. Enjoy the journey through rural Cambodia — rice paddies, sugar palms, and wooden stilt houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check in to a mid-range hotel in the riverside BKK1 or Riverside District (Daun Penh). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring stunning Khmer architecture, gilded spires, and a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles. Closed 11:30 AM–2:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the scenic Sisowath Quay (riverside promenade). Watch the sunset over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong river confluence — a magical golden-hour moment. Explore the lively riverside bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel breakfast or grab rice porridge (babor) from a local street stall before departure — $1–2.
meals.lunch: Bus stop meal or snacks en route. If flying, eat at Siem Reap airport or upon arrival in Phnom Penh.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a renowned social enterprise training street youth in hospitality. Excellent Khmer tapas-style dishes, $10–16 per person. Very popular; arrive early or book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance through Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — the most reliable operators with air conditioning and onboard WiFi. If flying, book through Cambodia Angkor Air or Bangkok Airways. Phnom Penh is more urban and hectic than Siem Reap — be mindful of traffic and keep valuables secure.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a detention and torture center by the Khmer Rouge between 1975–1979. An emotionally powerful and historically essential experience. Allow 2–3 hours. Hire an audio guide or survivor guide for deeper understanding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields), approximately 15 km south of the city. The memorial stupa contains thousands of skulls and the site offers a deeply moving audio tour narrated by survivors. Take a tuk-tuk ($8–12 round trip). Afterward, decompress at the National Museum of Cambodia near the Royal Palace — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome built in 1937, now a bustling market selling jewelry, clothing, and souvenirs. Enjoy the energy of Phnom Penh's evening riverside scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or try a local Phnom Penh breakfast spot for nom banh chok (Khmer noodles with green fish curry sauce) — a beloved local morning dish, $2–3.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the National Museum — try a set lunch at Romdeng Restaurant (another social enterprise) featuring traditional Cambodian cuisine with jungle ingredients, $10–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khéma La Poste or a riverside restaurant along Sisowath Quay. Try lok lak or a Cambodian BBQ (sach ko ang). Budget $12–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — take breaks as needed and be respectful of the space. Not recommended for young children. The National Museum closes on Mondays, so Sunday is ideal. Dress modestly at all memorial sites.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh for Sihanoukville by express bus (approximately 4 hours, $10–12) or private taxi ($60–80). Depart by 7:30–8:00 AM to maximize beach time. Alternatively, take a direct bus to Kep or Kampot for a quieter coastal experience — Kampot is highly recommended for its laid-back charm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot (recommended over Sihanoukville for mid-range, culturally rich travelers). Check in to a riverside guesthouse or boutique hotel. Explore Kampot's charming French colonial old town — colorful shophouses, riverside cafés, and the famous Kampot pepper plantations. Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) to explore at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River — magical views of Bokor Mountain and the mangroves as the sun dips below the horizon. Many guesthouses organize these for $5–8 per person. Fireflies often appear after dark along the riverbanks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh before departure.
meals.lunch: Eat at a rest stop en route or upon arrival in Kampot — try a riverside café for fresh spring rolls and Kampot pepper crab if budget allows ($8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or Epic Arts Café along the Kampot riverfront — relaxed atmosphere, good Khmer and Western fusion food, $8–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is a far better choice than Sihanoukville for mid-range cultural travelers. Sihanoukville has undergone significant development and its beach atmosphere has changed considerably. Kampot retains its colonial charm, natural beauty, and excellent food scene. Kep (30 minutes from Kampot) offers excellent seafood and quiet beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a former French colonial seaside resort town 25 km from Kampot. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market for the freshest Kampot pepper crab in Cambodia. Explore Kep National Park — a short hike through jungle to hilltop viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Thailand and nearby Vietnamese islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short boat ride from Kep to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — one of Cambodia's last undeveloped islands, with pristine white-sand beaches, turquoise waters, and hammocks strung between palm trees. Swim, snorkel, and relax on this peaceful island. Return to Kampot by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Kampot, visit a Kampot pepper farm for a late afternoon tour (several farms offer evening tours) — learn about Cambodia's world-famous pepper cultivation, taste different varieties, and purchase directly from farmers. Enjoy a quiet evening along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kampot guesthouse — many serve excellent fresh fruit platters, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Kep Crab Market — fresh grilled crab with Kampot pepper sauce is unmissable, $10–18 per person. One of Cambodia's great culinary experiences.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner back in Kampot at Baraka or a riverside night market stall. Try amok or grilled fish with Kampot pepper, $6–12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island boats run from Kep pier, taking about 20 minutes ($5–8 round trip). Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — rental is available on the island. The island has basic bungalows if you wish to overnight, but a day trip is sufficient. November weather should be perfect — clear skies and calm seas in the Gulf of Thailand.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot. Wake up early for a sunrise kayak or paddleboard on the Kampot River through the mangroves — a serene and memorable final Cambodian experience. Several operators offer guided sunrise kayak tours ($12–18 per person). Return for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Kampot for Phnom Penh International Airport by private taxi or bus (allow 3.5–4 hours). If your flight departs in the evening, you'll have time for a final stop at the Phnom Penh riverside for one last Cambodian coffee and reflection. Visit a local pharmacy or supermarket for any last-minute purchases (Kampot pepper, palm sugar, and dried mango make excellent gifts).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia with memories of ancient temples, floating villages, colonial riverside towns, and pristine island beaches. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast at a Kampot riverside café — try a strong Cambodian iced coffee (kafe tuk doh ko) with a fresh baguette and condensed milk, $3–5.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Phnom Penh near the airport or at a riverside restaurant if time allows — Khmer noodles or a rice dish, $5–8.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight departure for check-in and security at Phnom Penh International Airport. Book your Kampot-to-Phnom Penh taxi in advance through your guesthouse ($35–50 for a private car). Confirm all onward transport the evening before. Cambodia requires no airport departure tax — it's included in your ticket price. Ensure you have no Cambodian Riel left as it cannot be exchanged abroad — spend it or convert to USD at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your boutique property. Enjoy a welcome refreshment and a private orientation briefing with your dedicated concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to acclimatize. Optional: a relaxing dip in the pool before sunset.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cocktail experience on the hotel terrace overlooking the surrounding jungle canopy. Enjoy a curated welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine with modern presentation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread prepared by the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian spring rolls, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant — Amok Trei (fish amok in banana leaf), Lok Lak beef tenderloin, and a selection of artisan Cambodian desserts paired with curated wine

day_by_day.notes: Request a private airport transfer with a dedicated English-speaking guide. Confirm check-in arrangements in advance. Day 1 is intentionally light to allow rest after the long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private sunrise tour of Angkor Wat — arrive before the crowds for an exclusive viewing of the iconic temple reflected in the lotus pond. Accompanied by a specialist archaeologist-guide who provides in-depth historical context about the Khmer Empire.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the walled city of Angkor Thom, including the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Continue to Ta Prohm — the jungle temple famously featured in Lara Croft — where giant fig and silk-cotton trees embrace ancient stone galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa treatment — a traditional Khmer herbal compress massage to soothe temple-walking fatigue. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Siem Reap's French Quarter.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked croissants, Cambodian rice porridge (Bobor), tropical fruit platters, and barista-crafted coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel chef, served in a shaded pavilion within the Angkor complex — sandwiches, charcuterie, local cheeses, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Malis Restaurant (Siem Reap) — Cambodia's most celebrated fine-dining venue; try the 7-course tasting menu showcasing heritage Khmer recipes with contemporary technique

day_by_day.notes: Angkor Wat sunrise entry requires a valid Angkor Pass (3-day or 7-day recommended). Pre-book through your concierge. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees must be covered at all temple sites. Bring insect repellent and a sun hat.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the lesser-visited but extraordinary temples of the Angkor complex — Preah Khan, Neak Pean (a royal bathing temple on an island), and Ta Som. These sites offer a more intimate and crowd-free experience with remarkable bas-relief carvings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' a 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in the Angkor region. En route, stop at the Landmine Museum to understand Cambodia's recent history and ongoing humanitarian efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Apsara dance performance — arrange a private or semi-private classical Khmer dance show at a heritage venue, accompanied by a traditional Khmer set dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Cambodian Num Banh Chok (rice noodles with green fish curry sauce), eggs Benedict, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sala Lodges Restaurant near Siem Reap — farm-to-table Cambodian cuisine in a tranquil garden setting
meals.dinner: Private Apsara dinner at Koulen Restaurant or La Résidence d'Angkor — traditional Khmer banquet with live classical dance performance

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km from Angkor Wat — arrange a comfortable private vehicle. The Landmine Museum is a sobering but important cultural stop. Photography is permitted at most sites.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot air balloon ride over the Angkor Archaeological Park — a breathtaking aerial perspective of the temple complex stretching across the jungle canopy. Champagne served on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum in Siem Reap for a curated, air-conditioned deep-dive into Khmer civilization, art, and archaeology. Followed by a private cooking class at a luxury culinary school — learn to prepare three signature Cambodian dishes with a master chef.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant Pub Street area and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) with your guide. Browse artisan boutiques for silk scarves, lacquerware, and handcrafted jewelry. Dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the city.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-balloon breakfast at the hotel — pastries, yogurt, and coffee (balloon operators typically depart very early)
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during your cooking class as your gourmet lunch
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak — a Michelin-recommended restaurant in Siem Reap offering a seasonal tasting menu rooted in Cambodian culinary heritage

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon rides are weather-dependent — confirm the morning of. Book well in advance through your concierge. The cooking class should be pre-booked with a luxury culinary school such as Nénuphar or Le Tigre de Papier's premium program.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Cruise through floating villages, observe the unique ecosystem of stilted homes, floating schools, and fish farms. Accompanied by a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kampong Phluk floating village — a more authentic and less-touristed community on the lake. Explore narrow waterways by kayak or small wooden boat. Optional: visit a local family home for an insight into daily life on the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Evening at leisure — enjoy the hotel's infinity pool, spa, or a private yoga session arranged by the concierge. Optional: a private stargazing session in the Angkor grounds with a telescope and astronomer guide.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — eggs your way, Cambodian rice dishes, fresh juices, and a smoothie bar
meals.lunch: Lunch on the boat — a gourmet picnic basket prepared by the hotel with local seafood, rice dishes, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: In-room private dining experience — a curated 4-course Khmer menu served on your villa terrace under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Water levels on Tonlé Sap vary by season. November is post-rainy season — the lake is at its fullest and most spectacular. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sun protection for the boat excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Siem Reap Airport for a short domestic flight to Sihanoukville (or Koh Kong), then onward by private speedboat transfer to Koh Rong Sanloem — Cambodia's premier island destination with pristine white-sand beaches and crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a luxury eco-resort on Koh Rong Sanloem (e.g., Song Saa Private Island or Koh Rong Sanloem's top boutique resort). Spend the afternoon on the beach — snorkeling, paddleboarding, or simply relaxing on a sun lounger with a cocktail in hand.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach. Bioluminescent plankton night swim — a magical natural phenomenon unique to these waters, best experienced November through March.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at the island resort — grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and tropical salads
meals.dinner: Beachfront candlelit dinner at the resort — whole grilled fish, coconut curries, and fresh fruit sorbets with a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the domestic flight and speedboat transfer well in advance. Song Saa Private Island is the most exclusive option and offers a full-island private experience. Pack light resort wear, reef-safe sunscreen, and snorkel gear (though the resort provides equipment).

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's wellness instructor. Followed by a guided snorkeling excursion to the coral reefs surrounding the island — spot tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day island-hopping excursion by luxury speedboat to neighboring uninhabited islands. Swim in secluded coves, explore pristine beaches, and enjoy a champagne picnic on a sandbar.
day_by_day.evening: Spa afternoon — indulge in a signature island treatment using locally sourced ingredients such as coconut oil, lemongrass, and Cambodian herbs. Dinner at the resort's over-water restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Healthy beach breakfast — acai bowls, granola, tropical fruits, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Champagne picnic on a private sandbar — artisan sandwiches, fresh ceviche, tropical fruits, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Over-water dining experience at the resort — a 5-course seafood tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time for snorkeling and diving — visibility is typically excellent post-rainy season. Confirm marine conditions with the resort dive team. Reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory at most eco-resorts.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure on the island — optional activities include stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking through mangroves, deep-sea fishing, or simply relaxing in a hammock with a good book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer back to Sihanoukville and onward to Phnom Penh by private charter flight or luxury vehicle (approximately 4 hours by road with a private driver). Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh (e.g., Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal).
day_by_day.evening: Evening stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside promenade. Visit the illuminated Royal Palace exterior. Dinner at a premium restaurant in the city.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruits, and barista coffee overlooking the ocean
meals.lunch: Light lunch en route — stop at a curated riverside restaurant in Kampot if traveling by road
meals.dinner: Topaz Restaurant Phnom Penh — one of Cambodia's finest French-Cambodian fusion restaurants with an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The road from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh passes through Kampot — a charming riverside town worth a brief stop. A private charter flight (approximately 45 minutes) is the most comfortable option. Book Phnom Penh hotel well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring stunning Khmer architecture, sacred Buddha statues, and the famous Emerald Buddha. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.afternoon: A deeply moving and important cultural visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — essential for understanding Cambodia's tragic recent history under the Khmer Rouge. Accompanied by a specialist historian guide who provides sensitive, expert context.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Rosewood Phnom Penh's rooftop bar — panoramic views over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. Farewell dinner at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury hotel breakfast at Rosewood or Raffles — extensive buffet with live cooking stations and à la carte options
meals.lunch: Lunch at Khéma Restaurant Phnom Penh — an elegant French brasserie with refined Cambodian touches, popular with diplomats and discerning travelers
meals.dinner: Sora Sky Bar & Restaurant at Rosewood — rooftop dining with panoramic city views and a contemporary Asian menu

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. These sites are critically important to understanding Cambodian history and culture. An expert guide is strongly recommended. Dress respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Phnom Penh — visit the vibrant Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) for last-minute luxury souvenir shopping: silk scarves, handwoven textiles, gemstones, lacquerware, and fine Cambodian crafts. Your guide can help identify authentic, high-quality pieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: a private boat cruise on the Mekong River — a relaxing farewell to Cambodia's waterways. Alternatively, enjoy a final spa treatment at the hotel or a leisurely lunch by the riverside. Private transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for your onward flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. Farewell to Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor a full spread before your departure day begins
meals.lunch: Lunch at Raffles Hotel Le Royal's signature restaurant — a colonial-era landmark with timeless elegance and refined Cambodian-French cuisine; try their famous Femme Fatale cocktail
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight (depending on departure time)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Your concierge can arrange a private luxury airport transfer. Consider purchasing a curated gift box of Cambodian specialties — premium kampot pepper, artisan coffee, and silk — as souvenirs.
